advisory.what:
Several mutants are labelled `reachable` even though the only laws that can see them are REFUTED at baseline or are blocked by a premise. This means one I22 advisory is only partly fixed. Cases (spec/M2/lib/mutation_catalog_i60.json, mutants[].structural; rule at structural.M0):
- A148 and A162: the +1 copy of SequencerSetVerifyHash at common/batch/batch_header.go:226 and :254. Under the ssvh=0 premise of L_par_hdr_v0 and L_par_hdr_v1 (laws/M0/L_par_hdr_v0.json, assume), copy(batchBytes[186:], 0^32) produces exactly the original bytes, because byte 217 is overwritten afterwards. Only L_par_hdr_ssvh lacks the premise, and it is REFUTED.
- A165 to A168: the dropped length checks in validate() and Version(). L_rt_go_* apply ok_go and dec_go only to enc_sol outputs, which always have the exact length and are never empty. Only L_dom_hdr can see the change, and it is REFUTED.
- A081, probably: `version <= 2` becomes `< 2` at Rollup.sol:293. Only v2 laws can see it. L_par_hdr_v2 is REFUTED, and replay.semantics gives a reverted enc_sol 'no value' for L_rt_go_v2.
The structural rule ignores law premises (`assume`) and argument domains, so the stated ceiling of 103 is really at most 97 (96 with A081). The I22 reviews named these exact cases: fairness advisory 1 for drop_len_check, and soundness advisory 1(e)(f) for the ssvh copy at 186.
advisory.why: The kill rate does not change. Kills are decided per law at run time, and the run's survivor class is compared with the structural class. But these survivors will be filed as rule_gap/law_unmoved instead of masked, and the recorded ceiling is overstated. Fix: either extend the M0 'reads' rule to account for each law's assume clauses and argument domain, or list these 6 or 7 ids as known misclassifications under replaces.findings 'Limitations that stay'.

advisory.what: The catalog's own data decides exit (b) before anything runs, but the catalog never states the arithmetic. structural_counts.A gives 103 reachable (97 after the item above). Six mutants are equivalent by tce (I verified this by compiling all 122 Solidity mutants; exactly A110 to A113, A121 and A122 leave Rollup's deployed bytecode unchanged). That leaves at most 186 non-equivalent mutants. threshold.meets requires 5k >= 4n. With k <= 103 this needs n <= 128, which means at least 64 equivalent mutants, i.e. at least 58 more from the panel. With k <= 97 it needs at least 71.
advisory.why: This is not bias. The ceiling comes from the actual decision paths: M1x is decided on m1_view, M2 SORT-site laws on the hand model, and SORT-width laws can only be UNKNOWN. Those are the blind spots A1 is meant to expose, and the scope is the one the I22 fairness reviewer required. Still, whoever relies on the run should see in the catalog itself that exit (b) cannot be met unless the panel finds about a third of stratum A equivalent. The informative outputs are the per-operator, per-class and K1-only rates.

advisory.what:
How many variants each site gets correlates with whether it can be killed, and that raises the headline rate.
- 96 of the 103 reachable mutants come from two-variant operators (mstore_offset, shl_width, putuint64_offset, copy_offset, go_slice_offset).

Add a per-site line under reporting (a site counts as killed iff some variant is killed, with a non-equivalent denominator), so the Sensitivity number of whitepaper §12.1 is not read as uniform sensitivity.

advisory.what:
The duplicate-candidate rule (duplicates.rule) covers only statement-level operators on one line. It misses semantic duplicates across expression-level operators at the same store.
- A004 (mstore +1 at BatchHeaderCodecV0.sol:155) and A029 (shl 192 to 184 at the same line) give identical header bytes on every input. Byte 9 is always 0, written by storeBatchIndex's word at 1..32 in A004 and equal to (v>>64)&0xff = 0 for the uint16 numL1Messages in A029. Bytes 10..17 are equal. The tail is overwritten by storeTotalL1MessagePopped.
- A006 and A031 at :166 differ only when totalL1MessagePopped >= 2^64. That needs an owner to import a genesis header with a huge total (importGenesisBatch, Rollup.sol:226-252, does not check it), so the panel must decide.
- A002/A027 and A022/A033 differ through dirty memory at the new header pointer, so they are not duplicates.
advisory.why: This is small and affects both outcomes equally: one exact pair, possibly two. But it is the same kind of double counting the I22 review asked to flag (M046/M047). Widen the rule to 'mutants of any operators within one statement' so the panel sees {A001, A002, A027, A028}, {A003, A004, A029, A030}, {A005, A006, A031, A032} and {A021, A022, A033, A034}, and so the dedup rate covers them.

advisory.what:

- (a) The version byte has no literal offset, so neither language mutates it: BatchHeaderCodecV0.sol:133 mstore8(batchPtr,_version) and :46 mload(batchPtr); batch_header.go:217 and :245 batchBytes[0]=..., and :76 b[0].

- (c) The pointer-bump literals in the dataHash preimage are not mutated: Rollup.sol:872 add(dataPtr,8), :874 add(dataPtr,2), :940 add(_ptr,0x20).
- (d) In stratum B, copy and Put* calls with an explicit high bound match neither copy_offset/putuint64_offset nor go_slice_offset: batch_cache.go:1833-1849, consensus_message.go:110-118, batch_data.go:107.
advisory.why: All of this is plan-literal, and the effects are small and cancel partly. Gaps (a) and (b) are probably killable through the PAR and round-trip laws, so leaving them out lowers the rate slightly. Gap (c) would probably be projection_carried, so leaving it out raises the rate slightly. State them so the measured rate is not read as covering version-byte layout, Go comparison boundaries or pointer arithmetic.

advisory.what: Errors count as not killed in every denominator (kill_criterion.errors; reporting.rates: rate_all = killed/mutants). A Solidity mutant passes through far more steps than a Go mutant: two re-extractions, the projection, M0, the M1x differential, M2 derive and run, and Foundry harness builds. A Go mutant passes through one re-extraction, the projection, M0 and one Go replay.
advisory.why: This is conservative and consistent with the I22 S-B2 fix (errors are scoped to laws, and a kill takes precedence). But infrastructure failures pull the rate down unevenly by language. Add, beside each rate, the same rate over mutants that are not in error, and split rates by language: the 70 Go mutants all come from one file and are all 'reachable'.

advisory.what:
Three readings of the plan's verbatim kill criterion are resolved one way:
- K2(c) is stricter than 'a PROVED law loses its proof'.
- K1's two-sided replay plus baseline_finding is stricter than 'a witness that replays on the mutant code'.
- The K1 new-law clause is more liberal than 'a law moves to REFUTED'.
Separately, the plan maps 'swapped cursors' to 'the corpus' as well as to laws, while channels never decide a kill.
advisory.why: Each reading is justified by the plan's head clause ('the obstruction ... localized to the mutated edge') and by the I22 reviews. In practice the new-law channel is closed, because SORT-width laws can only be UNKNOWN, as stated. For transparency, report the plan-literal count (K1 or K2(a)+(b), without (c) and without the two-sided test) and the number of kills via new laws, next to the official rate. proof_lost_unwitnessed already appears per operator, so most of this can already be recomputed.

blocking.what: The replay harness for enc_sol is specified so that its inputs do not overlap the refuter's candidates, and the instrument gives no rule for the mismatch. Every K1 witness and every K2(c) falsification of every PROVED M0 law has to pass through this harness. So the kill outcome depends on a build choice nobody preregistered, and the literal readings of the spec give a kill rate of about 0.
blocking.why:
K1 needs a hit that replays on the mutant and not on the original. K2(c) needs a candidate that is false on the mutant and not false on the original.

All 5 PROVED M0 laws (L_par_hdr_v0, L_par_hdr_v1, L_rt_go_v0, L_rt_go_v1, L_rt_go_v2) call enc_sol: L_par_hdr compares against it and L_rt_go decodes its output. So all 103 'reachable' stratum-A mutants can only be killed through this harness, Go encoder and decoder mutants included. M1x and M2 are carried.

Under the spec's literal text, no candidate in the space can separate the mutant from the original. The rate would measure the harness, not HOLON's sensitivity. The only working reading is the store-level binding I16 used, and choosing it is a post-prereg decision that settles the outcome.

This also means two I22 fixes cannot work as written: S-B1, which makes K2(c) the localizer, and S-A4, 'exact field values through the tree's own code'.
blocking.evidence:
What the spec says:
- replay.m0 copies the source 'verbatim: the requires its revert paths name and the header build block up to the selected sink ... every other value bound from the witness through the extracted ops' field map'.
- roles.solidity.enc_sol.revert_lines are Rollup.sol:293, 294 and 295. In spec/M2/facts/morph_header.extracted.json, functions.enc_sol.paths gives :294 as 'previous state root is zero' (prevStateHash != 0) and :295 as 'new state root is zero' (postStateHash != 0).
- projection.enc_sol says 'A revert condition on a field other than the version is not projected'. So the model is defined exactly where the harness reverts.

The l1MessagePopped type mismatch:
- The copied block stores batchDataInput.numL1Messages (Rollup.sol:344). It is declared uint16 at IRollup.sol:20.
- The extracted Header records l1MessagePopped as value_type uint16, value_bits 16, width 8.
- The model's Header (facts/morph_header.json types.Header, copied by the projection) has an 8-byte l1MessagePopped. Assumption A-width allows values up to 2^64.

Recomputed with holon.refute.candidates and collect_pins on facts/morph_header.json, for L_par_hdr_v0, L_par_hdr_v1, L_par_hdr_ssvh, L_rt_go_v0 and L_rt_go_v2 (64 candidates each):
- The only candidates with prevStateHash != 0 and postStateHash != 0 are 'ones', '0x01', 'counting' and the 48 random headers.
- Every one of them has l1MessagePopped >= 2^16. So 0 of 64 candidates both execute and fit the code's types.
- In K2(c)'s window (the first 16 candidates) only 'ones', '0x01' and 'counting' execute.

What each literal reading gives:
- Truncating to uint16: the original enc_sol leaves bytes 9..14 zero, while enc_go_v0, enc_go_v1 and view keep all 8 bytes. The original code then falsifies every PROVED enc_sol law at every executable candidate. Every replaying hit is a baseline_finding and never K1. K2(c) requires 'not false on the original', so it never holds.
- Treating out-of-type values as 'no execution': no hit ever replays. Every law that moves to REFUTED becomes a replay_disagreement, which sets extraction_defect_detected. K2(c) never holds.

The contrast with I16:
- I16's harness (replay/M2/solidity/HolonCodec.t.sol:36-79; replay/M2/implementations.json edges.enc_sol.abi) binds l1MessagePopped as uint64 at the store call and copies no require.
- results/M2/refinement/enc_sol.json shows it agreed on 2107 of 2107 inputs, including boundary values with prev/post = 0 and l1 = 2^64-1.
- The 'construction tests against I16's committed real outputs' appear only in replaces.findings S-A4, not in the 'replay' section. They would contradict the instrument's own harness spec.

Also left unspecified:
- what a top-level role with no value means. In L_par_hdr_*, enc_sol reverts at prev/post = 0. replay.semantics covers only a role call 'inside another call'.
- which extracted document selects the copied statements and the field map: the null mutant's or the mutant's. If it is the mutant's, an extraction defect can enter both the model and the harness, and the two-sided replay stops being independent of the model under test.
blocking.fix:
Preregister a replacement whose replay.m0 pins down five things.
(1) enc_sol binds each store op's value argument from the witness at the Header field's width, as I16's abi does. The tree's own text is used for every other statement, so mutated Rollup lines such as :293, :334 and :352 still execute.
(2) The requires on fields the projection does not project are handled one of two ways: either leave them out of the harness, matching projection.enc_sol, or project them and restrict the refuter candidates, the hits and the K2(c) window to inputs that both trees execute.
(3) A top-level role call with no value is 'no execution'.
(4) The copied statements and the field map come from the null mutant's document, applied to each tree's text.
(5) A preregistered harness gate runs before any mutant, and if it fails nothing runs. On the null mutant, the harness must agree with the baseline model on every candidate of every M0 law where the model is defined, and must reproduce I16's committed enc_sol outputs. Planted controls must pass: a known mstore ±1 is K1-killed, and the null mutant shows no falsification.

advisory.what: not_K2's second sentence and the errors clause can erase a valid K1 kill, and read literally they misfile decided laws.
advisory.why:
The pipeline tries the proof first and refutes second (holon/pipeline.py:179-191). A proof-check timeout followed by a Bend-checked counter-law gives a genuine REFUTED.

But kill_criterion.not_K2 records 'a law PROVED at baseline ... whose proof attempt by the baseline generator did not complete with a non-null exit code and the marker SOME PROOFS FAIL' as error, and kill_criterion.errors makes 'a proof check timeout' an error of the law it decides.

Read literally, the same sentence also turns a law that stays PROVED on the mutant into 'error', because its attempt ended with 'ALL PROOFS CHECK'. Restrict the rule to laws that would otherwise end UNKNOWN. A law that is REFUTED with a checked counter-law is decided whatever happened to its proof attempt.

advisory.what: K2(b) cannot tell a checker rejection from a checker crash, and K2 localizes only at the code level.
advisory.why:
holon/bend.py:265-269 sets marker 'SOME PROOFS FAIL' for any non-zero exit, including a crash, a parse error or a type error in a generated model, even when the checker printed no verdict line. Condition (b) should require the checker's own first output line to be 'SOME PROOFS FAIL'.

(a) is per-law in name only for M0: law_sets.own_input hashes the whole projected document, so any projection change satisfies (a) for all 8 laws.

(c) still requires a real two-sided code falsification, so the counted defect is real. Still, the model's 'obstruction' is not tied to the same input. Optionally require that, at the (c) candidate, the mutant model's claim is undefined or false while the baseline model's claim is defined and true.

advisory.what: K2(c) can never witness a mutant that shrinks a domain, such as A081, so a real localized obstruction is classified proof_lost_unwitnessed.
advisory.why:
A081 flips Rollup.sol:293 from `version <= 2` to `< 2`, so every v2 commit reverts.

The extracted version bound becomes 1. The model's enc_sol is then undefined at the pinned version 2, and L_rt_go_v2 loses its proof. But replay.semantics makes enc_sol's revert on its own require 'no execution', so no candidate can be 'false on the mutant'.

The plan's verbatim 'or a PROVED law loses its proof' would count A081. Either state this in the limitations, or add a partiality witness: a candidate satisfying the law's premises at which the original executes and the mutant reverts on a revert line the role names.

advisory.what: survivor_classes has no class for replay_disagreement or baseline_finding.
advisory.why:
Such mutants fall through to the last rule, 'rule_gap (law_unmoved): ... kept its status', which is false for a law that moved to REFUTED. Meanwhile channels.flags sets extraction_defect_detected for the same mutant.

The plan files survivors as extraction gaps or rule gaps. A replay disagreement is an extraction gap, and a baseline finding is neither. Add classes for both. Under the blocking scenario, every reachable mutant would be filed as a rule gap.

advisory.what: The two-sided masked_obstruction test is blind behind L_par_hdr_v2 by construction.
advisory.why:
enc_go_v1 always writes version byte 1 (common/batch/batch_header.go:245) while enc_sol writes 2. Every v2 candidate is therefore already false on the original code, and 'replays on the mutant and not on the original' can never hold for that law.

State this as a limitation. Alternatively, define a masked obstruction as a grown difference set: bytes that differ on the mutant but not on the original at the same candidate.

advisory.what: The instrument never mentions I21, which the plan makes a dependency of I60.
advisory.why:
The §3 row lists I60's dependencies as I20, I18 and I21. I21's exit is 'zero open high-severity findings before I22', and its A2 attack targets the decoders' partiality, which is what the projection and the replay semantics read. I21 has not run yet: there is no docs/iterations/I21.md.

pins.why says a later change to a pinned artifact 'is a note, never a reason to recompute the catalog'. If I21's fixes change morph_header.extracted.json or morph_batch.go.extracted.json (walk_functions, revert_lines, ops), the frozen per-mutant edges, predicted sets and structural classes go stale while the run decides on the new documents. Obstructions on laws that only the new edges reach would then count as 'unpredicted'.

State I21's exit as a run precondition. Report, per mutant, the edges recomputed on the run's documents beside the frozen ones, along with any obstruction on a law that only the recomputed set predicts.

advisory.what: Nothing requires the null-mutant baseline to reproduce the recorded statuses.
advisory.why:
baseline.M0 records results/M0, which was decided on hand facts. K1 and K2 use the null-mutant run on the new projection. If the projection changes a status, for example a PROVED law becomes UNKNOWN, K2 is silently disabled for that law, and the structural classes no longer match.

Add a precondition: the projected null baseline reproduces 5 PROVED and 3 REFUTED; otherwise stop and report a projection defect, not a measurement.

advisory.what: The rules for contradicting an equivalence verdict are imprecise.
advisory.why:
'a baseline finding that replays on the mutant only' contradicts kill_criterion.baseline_finding, which by definition replays on both.

K1 and K2(c) witnesses are function-level. Their bound values, for example l1MessagePopped >= 2^16, may be unreachable through Rollup's public entry points, so a contradiction does not prove non-equivalence under equivalence.definition. Report function-level and reachable contradictions separately.

advisory.what: The (rule, subform, basis span) matching cannot match the two bvh_at site laws.
advisory.why:
In laws/M2/DERIVATION.json, laws[0] and laws[1] share (SORT, site, 'morph_rollup:bvh_at'). Matching requires 'exactly one', so a re-derived bvh_at law becomes 'new'. Its span is a hand-model definition, not a code location, so it can never be K1-eligible.

This has no effect today, because SORT-site laws are decided on the hand model, but it should be recorded.

advisory.what: The threshold outcome is fixed by construction, and the instrument states only the ceiling, not the consequence.
advisory.why:
structural_counts.A has 103 reachable mutants out of 192. Even if every reachable mutant is killed, 5*103 >= 4*(192-e) needs e >= 64 equivalent verdicts outside that class. tce supplies 6, so at least 58 more would be needed. M2 exit (b) is therefore effectively decided before the run.

This is legitimate under the plan ('the threshold never moves'), but the report should say so up front, so the rate is read as a sensitivity measurement and not as a pass/fail.
